purpose: Recheck the six discovery-index-only sources already present in the bounded 22-source inventory, bind their current default-branch revisions and selected Git objects, and preserve them as lead or mechanism references without bulk payload review, candidate promotion, installation, or execution.

cohortContract.coverageObjective: Determine whether the six pre-existing discovery indexes expose a specific incremental demand or mechanism gap that warrants child-source review, while preventing source popularity, catalog size, bundled installers, or control-plane claims from becoming candidate or manager authority.
cohortContract.accountAndDataBoundary: Public GitHub pages and Git objects only; no account connection, private repository access, credential use, service call, candidate runtime, or child-source acquisition.
cohortContract.inactiveIsolation: Blob-filtered no-checkout clones were created under one operating-system temporary root outside every Agent Skill, Plugin, App, MCP, Hook, manager, and consumer discovery root.
cohortContract.stopRule: Stop after exactly the six pre-existing discovery-index-only sources have a current default-branch revision, selected entry or license object identities, drift classification, and an index or mechanism-only disposition. Do not follow child links or add a candidate unless a separate demand-linked gap reopens targeted discovery.

limitations: The observation binds named default-branch revisions and selected Git objects on 2026-08-06; it does not prove future branch state or source health.
Tree counts and endpoint diffs are inventory evidence, not semantic review of every Skill, plugin, script, child repository, or generated projection.

Repository ownership, popularity, README claims, catalog inclusion, or an install command does not prove independent child provenance, instruction delivery, behavior, value, portability, security, or manager suitability.
The temporary root was sent to the Windows Recycle Bin after exact-path verification; recoverable Recycle Bin contents were not enumerated or permanently deleted.

sources.licenseDisposition: README declares Apache-2.0, no root license file was present, and the README says individual Skills may carry different licenses
staticFindings: The repository mixes a large lead index with bundled Skills and a plugin that connects external applications through an MCP gateway.
The entry documentation crosses API-key, authentication, external-service, account-data, plugin-installation, and real-action boundaries.
The source-level Apache declaration does not close the per-Skill license and child-source review boundary.
sources.futureRecheckTrigger: A naturally occurring integration task exposes a specific current-capability gap and binds one exact child or bundled item, account and data scope, service authority, fallback, and verification surface.

staticFindings: The GitHub-owned repository explicitly describes its agents, instructions, Skills, Hooks, workflows, and plugins as community-created contributions for GitHub Copilot.
The current revision materially changed plugin metadata and added or changed Skill paths, so the August 2 inventory is stale for counts and exact identity.
Its marketplace installation path and Copilot-specific carrier remain separate from CC Switch management and from current Codex or Claude behavior evidence.
sources.futureRecheckTrigger: A GitHub Copilot-specific task or portability comparison needs one exact item and separately binds community provenance, host support, installation, account, repository-write, and behavior boundaries.

sources.licenseDisposition: MIT root license; nested and generated projections still require item-specific dependency and provenance review
staticFindings: The repository is a large multi-domain, multi-host payload catalog with generated host projections, hundreds of scripts, plugins, Hooks, MCP configuration, and direct installers.
Advertised cross-host support and projection counts are source claims, not host exposure, invocation, behavior, or portability evidence.
Direct npx, curl, clone, and install-script routes do not preserve the current CC Switch SSOT, database, backup, enablement, update, or consumer-projection lifecycle.
sources.futureRecheckTrigger: A mapped demand gap names one exact canonical item and warrants item-level source, generated-projection, dependency, security, manager-import, and host-behavior review.

staticFindings: The repository remains a README-based lead index with no local SKILL.md payloads.
The current drift is limited to six README insertions, so it does not supply a new local payload or manager mechanism.
Official-team and community labels remain discovery metadata; every linked child source requires independent exact identity, license, dependency, account, and behavior review.
sources.futureRecheckTrigger: A specific demand-linked gap selects one child source after current native, official runtime, managed, and composed routes are rechecked.

sources.licenseDisposition: MIT for original code and tooling; CC BY 4.0 for original non-code content; third-party notices and exceptions remain item-specific
staticFindings: The repository now presents a local read-only MCP and CLI planning layer, full catalog, plugins, bundles, Workbench, direct installers, generated compatibility projections, and experimental apply or recovery paths as one external control-plane ecosystem.
The current revision materially changed catalog, plugin metadata, executable code, and Skill paths; count growth is not demand coverage, independent source review, suitability, or value evidence.

Its catalog, selection, planning, and evidence mechanisms are eligible only as exact future comparators; bulk acquisition, direct installation, MCP activation, or manager substitution remains outside this cohort.
sources.futureRecheckTrigger: A bounded mechanism gate needs an exact comparator for catalog search, selection evidence, immutable planning, or recovery and separately binds MCP, CLI, filesystem, manager, license, and execution authority.

staticFindings: The source remains a curated README list with rankings and copy-ready direct install commands but no local Skill payloads.
Preference labels and concise descriptions are lead metadata, not independent quality, source identity, dependency, security, instruction-delivery, behavior, or value evidence.
Direct installer commands do not preserve CC Switch lifecycle authority.
sources.futureRecheckTrigger: A mapped demand gap names one child source and the child is independently reviewed at an exact revision before any manager or task-time state transition.

portfolioDecision.nextAction: Return to current demand and source authorities. Reopen exactly one child or mechanism only after a specific mapped gap or material source or host change is bound; otherwise select another bounded mechanism-only gate without expanding candidate names.
